title: A prenatal exercise visit, a headache and spots in her vision
objective: Stop exercise in pregnancy for warning signs (painful contractions, vaginal bleeding, dyspnea, dizziness, headache, chest or calf pain) and respect absolute contraindications such as placenta previa, preterm labor and preeclampsia
secondaryObjectives: Prescribe exercise in pregnancy (about 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, checked with the talk test), avoiding the supine position, contact sports, fall-risk sports and altitude changes such as scuba diving

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. Preeclampsia is new or worsening hypertension with proteinuria after 20 weeks; severe features include systolic BP of 160 mm Hg or more and/or diastolic 110 or more, 'new-onset headache unresponsive to medication and not accounted for by alternative diagnoses', visual disturbances and severe persistent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain. Eclampsia is unexplained generalized seizures with preeclampsia, and 'sometimes eclampsia occurs before a diagnosis of preeclampsia is made'. Severe features are managed in hospital.

brief.situation: 15:00 in an outpatient pelvic health clinic. You are the physical therapist. Ms. Alvarez, 32, is 35 weeks pregnant with her first baby and is here for her third visit for pelvic girdle pain. Today's plan: a supervised exercise session and her home program.
handover: Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated so far, she says. Her blood pressure was normal at her obstetric visit two weeks ago.
Last visit she rode the recumbent bike for 10 minutes and did hip and core strengthening without trouble.
Clinic policy: an urgent pregnancy concern goes to the hospital's labor and delivery triage unit, which takes calls from clinicians; 911 for transport when she should not travel by car.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time at the pace you choose: study pace (3x) or exam realism (1x). Pause any time.
Each question or measurement takes the time on its button. Decide what to check, what it means and what to do.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Untreated, the preeclampsia worsens toward a seizure in about an hour from the start of the visit. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
Exercise raises her blood pressure and brings the authored seizure point closer. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
The authored point at which an eclamptic seizure occurs if she is still in the clinic. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
A question set or a bedside check: about 1 min.
A seated blood pressure with the right cuff after she has sat quietly: about 2 min.
EMS reaches the clinic about 10 min after a 911 call.

why.question: Is it safe to exercise today? What do her findings suggest, and what do you do now?

parts.label: Findings
parts.criteria: Names the severe-range blood pressure (160 systolic or 110 diastolic or more, confirmed on a repeat reading), the headache not helped by acetaminophen, the visual spots and the new swelling at 35 weeks as possible preeclampsia with severe features; says exercise is contraindicated.
parts.modelAnswer: No exercise today. At 35 weeks she has a severe-range blood pressure that held on a repeat reading, a headache since morning that acetaminophen did not help, spots in her vision and new swelling. That is possible preeclampsia with severe features, which is a contraindication to exercise and an emergency.

parts.label: Action
parts.criteria: Stops all exercise; rests her on her left side and stays with her; calls labor and delivery triage now and 911 for transport rather than a private car or a message; tells her obstetric provider.
parts.modelAnswer: Stop the session, rest her on her left side and stay with her. Call labor and delivery triage now with the readings and symptoms and call 911 to take her, because she could seize on the way. Then tell her obstetric provider's office what I found.

expertPath.text: Before any exercise, ask about warning symptoms: a headache acetaminophen did not help and spots in her vision. Stop: no exercise today.
Seated blood pressure with the right cuff: severe range. Repeat it a few minutes later: still severe. Look at the swelling.
Rest her on her left side. Call labor and delivery triage with the numbers and 911 to take her. Stay with her.
Tell her obstetric provider's office. EMS arrives about 15:16.

seizure.headline: She seized in the clinic
seizure.body: A headache that medicine does not help and visual spots in late pregnancy are warning signs. Measure the pressure, stop the session and get her to labor and delivery by EMS at once.

sentFast.headline: Warning signs found; sent by 911
sentFast.body: You screened before exercising, confirmed a severe-range pressure with symptoms, stopped, positioned her on her side and sent her by EMS to labor and delivery. That is the expert path.

sentSlow.headline: Sent, by a slower or riskier route
sentSlow.body: Check the route (EMS, not a private car), how long after the first warning sign you called, whether you confirmed the pressure, and whether any exercise happened after a warning sign.

time_up.headline: Still in the clinic
time_up.body: Exercise is not the priority when a warning sign appears. Stop, measure and send.

scoring.modelReasoning: Exercise in pregnancy is safe without complications, but it stops for warning signs, and preeclampsia is an absolute contraindication. At 35 weeks a headache unresponsive to acetaminophen, visual spots, new swelling and a blood pressure of 160/110 or more confirmed within minutes point to preeclampsia with severe features, which is managed in hospital. Stop the session, rest her on her left side (never supine late in pregnancy), call labor and delivery triage and send her by EMS because a seizure can come before the diagnosis is made, then tell her obstetric provider.

bpQ.ask: While you wait: which blood pressure reading in pregnancy is in the severe range?
bpQ.explain: A systolic pressure of 160 or more or a diastolic of 110 or more is severe range; it can be confirmed on a repeat reading within minutes.
